questions.q: What three things does a strong resume bullet name explicitly, according to this lesson's formula?
options: The course title, the instructor's name, and the completion date
The action taken, the system or area it was done in, and the resulting outcome
Only the name of the software, repeated three times
The company's revenue, employee count, and founding year
questions.explain: The action-system-outcome formula names what you did, where you did it, and what resulted - far stronger than a vague restatement of a course title.

questions.q: Why is "Learned Oracle Fusion General Ledger" a weak resume bullet?
options: It mentions a specific Oracle product by name
It is too long for a resume
It names no specific action, system detail, or outcome - it's a vague restatement rather than a provable claim
It uses too many technical abbreviations
questions.explain: The bullet gives no specifics - what was actually configured, in what structure, with what result - making it forgettable and unconvincing.

questions.q: How should hands-on practice-environment work be described on a resume, according to this lesson?
options: As identical to paid client or production experience, with no distinction made
It should never be mentioned on a resume at all
Accurately, as structured training-environment work - which can still be described as a real, substantive skill without claiming client experience
Only in vague, unspecific language so no one notices it wasn't client work
questions.explain: The lesson recommends precise, honest framing: describe it as training-environment work, which still reads as substantive without overclaiming client experience.

questions.q: What is the main risk of claiming client or production experience you don't actually have?
options: There is no real risk as long as the resume looks professional
It only matters for very senior roles, never for entry-level ones
It makes the resume bullet too short
It is the fastest way to lose credibility once an interviewer asks a natural follow-up question
questions.explain: Inflated claims tend to collapse under a simple, natural follow-up question, which damages credibility far more than an honestly framed bullet would have.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of the action-system-outcome formula applied correctly?
options: "Diagnosed and corrected an unreversed GRNI accrual causing an AP aging-to-GL mismatch during a simulated month-end close"
"Took an Oracle Payables course"
"Interested in Oracle Financials"
"Familiar with accounting software in general"
questions.explain: This bullet names the action (diagnosed and corrected), the system detail (GRNI accrual, AP aging-to-GL), and the outcome (resolved during a simulated close).
